headline: Burnley are 22nd — and still favourites at Lincoln
summary: Lincoln lost 0-6 at home to West Ham this month and are still chasing a first home win of the season; they have lost three of their last five. Burnley arrive 22nd with one win in 11, Nicky Hayen under pressure and 15 players ruled out, though he is reported to be in the dugout. Even so, on the market average with the margin removed, Burnley are 41.7% to win, against Lincoln's 31.8%. The handicap tells the closer story: Lincoln get a head start of 0.25 goals, and the fair goals line is 2.53. Burnley are favoured — but only just.
read: Two Championship strugglers meet at Sincil Bank: Burnley are 22nd, a year without a home league win and with a manager under pressure, yet still rated 41.7% to win away. Lincoln are 18th, still without a home win and hit for six by West Ham this month, but a handicap fair line of about +0.2 goals and a 2.53 goals total say the market sees a tight, close-to-even game.

facts.fact: The market makes Burnley 41.7% to win at Sincil Bank, well clear of Lincoln at 31.8%.
facts.meaning: The away side are clear favourites, but with a big slice of the probability sitting outside a Burnley win, this is not priced as a one-sided game.

facts.fact: Burnley manager Nicky Hayen is under growing pressure after one win in his first 11 games, though he is reported to be in the dugout at Lincoln.
facts.meaning: A manager fighting for his job takes the division's 22nd-placed side into a game they are still expected to win.

facts.fact: Burnley's early team news for the Lincoln trip lists 15 players ruled out and one fitness doubt.
Burnley have gone a full year without a home league win, a run extended by Saturday's 1-2 defeat to Wolves.
facts.meaning: Their season is being kept alive by draws rather than wins, and they arrive at Lincoln from the bottom three.

facts.fact: Lincoln lost 0-6 at home to West Ham on 14 October.
facts.meaning: Lincoln are 18th and still chasing a first home win of the season — the home form is the weak spot in their record.

facts.fact: On the handicap the market rates Burnley only about a fifth of a goal better, with Lincoln +0.25 a 51.8% shot.
facts.meaning: Despite Burnley being the clear match favourite, on the line this is priced as close to an even game — the draw and a narrow Burnley win are the market's main outcomes.

facts.fact: Lincoln out-created Swansea 2.11 to 0.92 in September and still lost 1-2; they also out-created Sheffield United 1.39 to 0.68 and lost 0-3.
facts.meaning: Two of Lincoln's defeats came in games they created more than the opposition, so their league position is not simply a story of being outplayed.

facts.fact: The market has the goals fair line at 2.53, with Over 2.5 at 50.8% — effectively a coin flip.
facts.meaning: There is no strong lean on total goals, so this is priced as a game that could go either way on scoring.

sources.fact: Burnley manager Nicky Hayen is reported to be expected in the dugout for the Lincoln match despite growing pressure, having won just one of his first 11 games.

Lincoln won their appeal against Deji Elerewe's red card from the Millwall match, making him available.
